newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran bans foreign names for places, businesses.
newsitem.headline: Iran bans foreign names for places, businesses.

text.p: A powerful Iranian state cultural body has banned the use of foreign names for businesses and public places, in a further step in the country's fight against a Western "cultural invasion", a newspaper said on Thursday.

A directive by the Supreme Council for Cultural Revolution said workplaces, businesses and other public places should be named after "great cultural, literary, scientific, political and revolutionary personalities of Islam, Iran and the (1979) Islamic revolution", the daily Ettelaat said.

Such places could also be named after "cities and famous historical sites and the Islamic revolution's martyrs and important events", said the council, which is Iran's highest cultural decision-making body.

Also acceptable were names of "natural beauties of Iran and mythologcal names acceptable to the people", it said. "Stores, firms and workplaces should not use foreign names and all names should belong to the Persian language."
Foreign names would be approved by authorities only if their use aimed to further ties with other countries, it added.

The rules were part of Iran's fight against Western influences which it condemns as a "cultural invasion". They would not affect the use of Arabic names, seen by authorities as part of a common Islamic heritage.
Iran has held several similar campaigns in the past few years, but has had limited success in curbing the wide use of Western signs and characters on products, clothing and shop windows.
